163.h: 68 - Abū al-Dardāʾ ʿUwaymir ibn Zayd ibn Qays al-Anṣārī * (ع)
163.t:
the Imam (الإمام), the exemplar (القدوة), the judge (القاضي) of Damascus, and companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū al-Dardāʾ, ʿUwaymir ibn Zayd ibn Qays.
It is also said: ʿUwaymir ibn ʿĀmir.
It is also said: son of ʿAbd Allāh.
And it was said: son of Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī.
The sage of this Ummah, and the master of the reciters (القارئ) in Damascus.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: He is ʿUwaymir ibn Qays ibn Zayd ibn Qays (2) ibn Umayyah ibn ʿĀmir ibn ʿAdī ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj.
He said: It is also said that his name is ʿĀmir ibn Mālik.
He narrated several hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ. ⟦2:335⟧
He is counted among those who recited to the Prophet ﷺ, and it has never reached us that he recited to anyone else.
He is counted among those who gathered the Qurʾān in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He took up the teaching of recitation in Damascus during the caliphate of ʿUthmān, and before that.
Narrating from him: أنس بن مالك، وفضالة بن عبيد، وابن عباس، وأبو أمامة، وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص، وغيرهم من جلة الصحابة، وجبير بن نفير، وزيد بن وهب، وأبو إدريس الخولاني، وعلقمة بن قيس، وقبيصة بن ذؤيب، وزوجته؛ أم الدرداء العالمة، وابنه؛ بلال بن أبي الدرداء، وسعيد بن المسيب، وعطاء بن يسار، ومعدان بن أبي طلحة، وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي، وخالد بن معدان، وعبد الله بن عامر اليحصبي (1) .
It was said that he recited the Qurʾān to him and met him; if that is true, then perhaps he recited part of the Qurʾān to him while he was a boy.
Those who recited to him: عطية بن قيس، وأم الدرداء.
Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī said: Those who presented the Qurʾān to him: خليد بن سعد، وراشد بن سعد، وخالد بن معدان، وابن عامر.
So said al-Dānī.
He took charge of the judgeship in Damascus during the reign of ʿUthmān, so he is the first of its judges mentioned to us. His house was at Bāb al-Barīd; then, in the reign of Sultan Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn, it came to be known as Dār al-Ghazzī (2) . ⟦2:336⟧
179 hadiths are narrated from him.
The two of them agreed on two hadiths of his.
Al-Bukhārī alone has three, and Muslim alone eight.
Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated from Mughīth ibn Sumayy:
That Abū al-Dardāʾ ʿUwaymir ibn ʿĀmir was of the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj.
Ibn Isḥāq said on one occasion: He is ʿUwaymir ibn Thaʿlabah.
He died three years before ʿUthmān (1) .
Al-Bukhārī said: I asked a man from the descendants of Abū al-Dardāʾ, and he said: His name is ʿĀmir ibn Mālik, and his nickname is ʿUwaymir (2) .
Abū Mushir said: He is ʿUwaymir ibn Thaʿlabah.
Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Shaybah and a number of others said: ʿUwaymir ibn ʿĀmir (3) .
The last who claimed to have seen Abū al-Dardāʾ was an old man who lived until the reign of al-Rashīd.
Abū Ibrāhīm al-Tarjumānī said: Isḥāq Abū al-Ḥārith narrated to us; he said:
I saw Abū al-Dardāʾ: he had an aquiline nose and blue-grey eyes, and he dyed his hair with yellow (4) .
روى: الأعمش، عن خيثمة، قال أبو الدرداء:
I was a merchant before the Prophetic mission. When Islam came, I tried to combine trade and worship, but they would not go together, ⟦2:337⟧ so I abandoned trade and devoted myself to worship (1) .
I say: The best is to combine both matters together with jihad. What he said is the way of a group of the Salaf (السلف) and the Sufis (الصوفي). There is no doubt that people's temperaments differ in this: some are strong enough to combine them, like al-Ṣiddīq and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and as Ibn al-Mubārak was; some are unable and confine themselves to worship; and some are strong at the beginning and then become unable, or the reverse. All of this is permissible, but fulfilling the rights of the wife and the household is indispensable.
Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: Abū al-Dardāʾ accepted Islam on the day of Badr, then took part in Uḥud. On that day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to drive back those who were on the mountain, and he drove them back by himself. His acceptance of Islam had come somewhat late (2) .
Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd al-Ḥimṣī said: When the companions of the Messenger of Allah were routed on the day of Uḥud, Abū al-Dardāʾ was that day among the people who rallied back to the Messenger of Allah. When the polytheists loomed over them from above, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O Allah, they have no right to be above us) .
People rallied to him and volunteered, among them ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ, until they drove them from their position; and Abū al-Dardāʾ acquitted himself well that day.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (What an excellent horseman ʿUwaymir is) (3) . ⟦2:338⟧
And he said: (The sage of my Ummah is ʿUwaymir) .
This was narrated by: يحيى البابلتي، حدثنا صفوان بن عمرو، عن شريح (1) .
Thābit al-Bunānī and Thumāmah, from Anas:
The Prophet ﷺ died and no one had gathered the Qurʾān except four: Abū al-Dardāʾ, Muʿādh, Zayd ibn Thābit and Abū Zayd (2) .
Zakariyyā and Ibn Abī Khālid said, from al-Shaʿbī:
Six gathered the Qurʾān in the time of the Messenger of Allah, all of them from the Anṣār: Muʿādh, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Zayd, Abū Zayd, Ubayy and Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd (3) .
Mujammiʿ ibn Jāriyah had one or two surahs remaining when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died (4) . ⟦2:339⟧
Ismāʿīl, from al-Shaʿbī, who said:
Ibn Masʿūd had taken seventy-odd surahs —meaning: from the Prophet ﷺ— and learned the rest from Mujammiʿ; and none of the caliphs among the Companions (الصحابي) gathered the Qurʾān except ʿUthmān (1) .
Abū al-Zāhiriyyah said: Abū al-Dardāʾ was among the last of the Anṣār to accept Islam (2) . He used to worship an idol, and Ibn Rawāḥah and Muḥammad ibn Maslamah entered his house and smashed his idol.
He returned and began gathering up the idol, saying: Woe to you! Why did you not resist? Why did you not defend yourself?
Umm al-Dardāʾ said: If it could benefit or defend anyone, it would have defended itself and benefited itself.
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: Prepare water for me in the washing place.
He washed, put on his garment, and then went to the Prophet ﷺ.
Ibn Rawāḥah saw him coming and said: O Messenger of Allah! This is Abū al-Dardāʾ, and I think he has only come looking for us.
He said: (He has only come to accept Islam; my Lord promised me concerning Abū al-Dardāʾ that he would accept Islam (3)) .
The part of his words from (“He used to worship …” to the end) was narrated by: معاوية بن صالح، عن أبي الزاهرية، عن جبير بن نفير.
Part of it was narrated by: أبو صالح، عن معاوية، عن أبي الزاهرية، عن جبير، عن ⟦2:340⟧ أبي الدرداء:
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Allah promised me the Islam of Abū al-Dardāʾ, and he accepted Islam (1)) .
Abū Mushir narrated from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz:
That Abū al-Dardāʾ accepted Islam on the day of Badr and took part in Uḥud, and ʿUmar assigned him four hundred —meaning per month— placing him with the Badrīs (البدري).
Al-Wāqidī said: It was said that he did not take part in Uḥud.
Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Makḥūl:
The Companions (الصحابي) used to say: The most merciful of us toward us is Abū Bakr, the most outspoken of us with the truth is ʿUmar, our trustworthy one is Abū ʿUbaydah, the most knowledgeable of us about the lawful and the unlawful is Muʿādh, the best reciter among us is Ubayy, and a man who has knowledge is Ibn Masʿūd; and ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ followed them in intellect (2) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: The Companions (الصحابي) used to say: The one of us who most follows knowledge and practice is Abū al-Dardāʾ (3) .
ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfah narrated from his father:
That the Messenger of Allah made Salmān and Abū al-Dardāʾ brothers. Salmān came to visit him and found Umm al-Dardāʾ in shabby clothes.
He said: What is the matter with you?
She said: Your brother has no need of this world; he stands in prayer all night and fasts all day.
Abū al-Dardāʾ came, welcomed him, and set food before him.
Salmān said to him: Eat.
He said: I am fasting.
He said: I adjure you to break your fast.
So he ate with him, then he spent the night with him. When it was night, Abū al-Dardāʾ wanted to get up, but Salmān prevented him and said: ⟦2:341⟧
Your body has a right over you, your Lord has a right over you, and your family has a right over you. Fast and break your fast, pray, go to your wife, and give everyone who has a right his right.
When it was near dawn, he said: Get up now if you wish.
So they both got up, performed ablution, prayed, and then went out to the prayer. Abū al-Dardāʾ drew near to tell the Messenger of Allah what Salmān had told him.
He said to him: (O Abū al-Dardāʾ! Your body has a right over you, just as Salmān told you (1)) .
البابلتي: حدثنا الأوزاعي، حدثنا حسان بن عطية، قال:
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: If I forgot a verse and found no one to remind me of it except a man in Bark al-Ghimād, I would travel to him (2) .
الأعمش: عن سالم بن أبي الجعد، عن أبي الدرداء، قال:
Ask me, for by Allah, if you lose me you will lose a great man of the Ummah of Muḥammad (3) ﷺ.
ربيعة القصير: عن أبي إدريس، عن يزيد بن عميرة، قال:
When death came to Muʿādh, they said: Give us counsel.
He said: Knowledge and faith remain in their place; whoever seeks them will find them —he said it three times— so seek knowledge with four: with ʿUwaymir Abū ⟦2:342⟧ al-Dardāʾ, Salmān, Ibn Masʿūd, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who had been a Jew and then accepted Islam (1) .
From Ibn Masʿūd: The scholars of the people are three: one in Iraq, another in Syria —meaning Abū al-Dardāʾ— and he needs the one in Iraq —meaning himself— and both of them need the one in Medina —meaning ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) (2) —.
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is weak (ضعيف).
ابن وهب: أخبرني يحيى بن عبد الله، عن عبد الرحمن الحجري، قال:
Abū Dharr said to Abū al-Dardāʾ: The dusky earth has not carried, nor has the green sky shaded, anyone more knowledgeable than you, O Abū al-Dardāʾ (3) .
منصور: عن رجل، عن مسروق، قال:
I found that the knowledge of the Companions (الصحابي) culminated in six: ʿUmar, ʿAlī, Ubayy, Zayd, Abū al-Dardāʾ and Ibn Masʿūd; then their knowledge culminated in ʿAlī and ʿAbd Allāh (4) .
Khālid ibn Maʿdān said: Ibn ʿUmar used to say: Tell us about the two men of intellect.
It would be said: Who are the two men of intellect?
He would say: Muʿādh and Abū al-Dardāʾ (5) . ⟦2:343⟧
Saʿd ibn Isḥāq narrated from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, who said:
Five gathered the Qurʾān: Muʿādh, ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ubayy and Abū Ayyūb. In the time of ʿUmar, Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān wrote to him:
The people of Syria have become numerous and have filled the cities, and they need someone to teach them the Qurʾān and give them understanding, so help me with men who will teach them.
ʿUmar summoned the five and said: Your brothers have asked my help for someone to teach them the Qurʾān and give them understanding in the religion, so help me, may Allah have mercy on you, with three of you if you are willing; and if three of you volunteer, let them go out.
They said: We will not cast lots; this one is a very old man —of Abū Ayyūb— and as for this one, he is ill —of Ubayy.
So Muʿādh, ʿUbādah and Abū al-Dardāʾ went out.
ʿUmar said: Begin with Ḥimṣ, for you will find the people there in different states; among them is one who learns quickly, so when you see that, direct a group of the people to him, and when you are satisfied with them, let one of you stay there, and let one go out to Damascus and the other to Palestine.
He said: They came to Ḥimṣ and stayed there until, when they were satisfied with the people, ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit remained there, Abū al-Dardāʾ went out to Damascus, and Muʿādh to Palestine, where he died in the plague of ʿAmwās.
Later ʿUbādah moved to Palestine and died there, and Abū al-Dardāʾ remained in Damascus until he died (1) . ⟦2:344⟧
Al-Aḥwaṣ ibn Ḥakīm, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, who said:
It reached ʿUmar that Abū al-Dardāʾ had built a shelter in Ḥimṣ, so he wrote to him:
O ʿUwaymir, was what the Byzantines built not enough for you, without adorning the world, when Allah has decreed its ruin? When my letter reaches you, move to Damascus (1) .
Mālik, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, who said:
When Abū al-Dardāʾ had judged between two people and they turned away from him, he would look at them and say:
Come back to me; repeat your case to me (2) .
معمر: عن الأعمش، عن عمرو بن مرة، عن ابن أبي ليلى، قال:
Abū al-Dardāʾ wrote to Maslamah ibn Mukhallad: Peace be upon you. To proceed: when the servant acts in disobedience to Allah, Allah hates him, and when Allah hates him, He makes him hateful to His servants (3) .
Abū Wāʾil said, from Abū al-Dardāʾ:
I command you to do something that I do not do myself, but perhaps Allah will reward me for it.
شعبة: عن سعد بن إبراهيم، عن أبيه:
That ʿUmar said to Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Dharr and Abū al-Dardāʾ: What is this narrating of hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
And I reckon he kept them confined in Medina until he was struck down (4) . ⟦2:345⟧
Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Muslim ibn Mishkam:
Abū al-Dardāʾ said to me: Count those who are in our gathering.
He said: They came to one thousand six hundred and some. They would recite, competing with one another ten by ten. When he had prayed the dawn prayer, he would turn round and recite a portion, and they would gather round him, listening to his wording; and Ibn ʿĀmir was foremost among them (1) .
وقال هشام بن عمار: حدثنا يزيد بن أبي مالك، عن أبيه، قال:
Abū al-Dardāʾ would pray, then teach recitation and recite himself, until, when he wanted to get up, he would say to his companions: Is there a wedding feast or an ʿaqīqah (2) for us to attend?
If they said yes, so be it; otherwise he would say: O Allah, I call You to witness that I am fasting. He is the one who instituted these circles for recitation.
Al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Abū al-Dardāʾ was among those who were given knowledge (3) .
Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, who said:
I sounded out the companions of Muḥammad ﷺ and found that their knowledge culminated in: ʿUmar, ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Muʿādh, Abū al-Dardāʾ and Zayd ibn Thābit (4) .
From Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: Abū al-Dardāʾ is among the scholars and jurists (الفقيه) who cure the disease (5) . ⟦2:346⟧
وقال الليث: عن رجل، عن آخر:
I saw Abū al-Dardāʾ enter the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ with a following like that of a ruler: some asking about an inheritance share, some asking about arithmetic, some asking about a hadith, some asking about a difficult problem, and some asking about poetry.
Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd al-Qaṣīr said: When Abū al-Dardāʾ narrated from the Messenger of Allah, he would say: O Allah, if not like this, then something like it (1) .
Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd:
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: Why do I see your scholars departing while your ignorant ones do not learn? Learn, for the scholar and the learner are partners in the reward (2) .
From Abū al-Dardāʾ by a mursal (مرسل) route: You will not be a scholar until you are a learner, and you will not be a learner until you act upon what you know. What I fear most, when I stand for the reckoning, is that it will be said to me: What did you do with what you knew (3) ?
Jaʿfar ibn Burqān, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān:
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: Woe once to the one who does not know, and woe seven times to the one who knows and does not act (4) . ⟦2:347⟧
Ibn ʿAjlān, from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh:
I said to Umm al-Dardāʾ: Which worship of Abū al-Dardāʾ was most frequent?
She said: Reflection and taking heed (1) .
From Abū al-Dardāʾ: An hour of reflection is better than a night of standing in prayer (2) .
ʿAmr ibn Wāqid, from Ibn Ḥalbas:
It was said to Abū al-Dardāʾ —and he never slackened in remembrance of Allah—: How many times do you glorify Allah each day?
He said: A hundred thousand, unless the fingers make a mistake (3) .
الأعمش: عن عمرو بن مرة، عن أبي البختري، قال:
While Abū al-Dardāʾ was lighting a fire under a pot of his, a sobbing sound was heard in the pot, like the sound of a child; then the pot tipped over, then returned to its place without anything spilling from it.
Abū al-Dardāʾ began calling: O Salmān! Look at something the like of which neither you nor your father has ever seen.
Salmān said to him: Had you kept silent, you would have heard of the greatest signs of your Lord (4) .
Al-Awzāʿī, from Bilāl ibn Saʿd:
That Abū al-Dardāʾ said: I seek refuge with Allah from the dispersion of the heart.
It was said: And what is the dispersion of the heart?
He said: That I should be given wealth in every valley (5) . ⟦2:348⟧
It is narrated from Abū al-Dardāʾ that he said: Were it not for three things, I would not love to remain alive for an hour: thirst in the midday heat, prostration at night, and sitting with people who pick out the best of speech as the choicest fruits are picked out (1) .
الأعمش: عن غيلان، عن يعلى بن الوليد، قال:
I met Abū al-Dardāʾ and said: What do you wish for those you love?
He said: Death.
I said: And if he does not die?
He said: That his wealth and his children become few (2) .
Muʿāwiyah ibn Qurrah said: Abū al-Dardāʾ said:
Three things I love while people dislike them: poverty, illness and death. I love poverty out of humility to my Lord, death out of longing for my Lord, and illness as an expiation for my sins (3) .
الأوزاعي: عن يحيى بن أبي كثير، عن أبيه: That Abū al-Dardāʾ's eye pained him until its sight was gone.
It was said to him: Why not supplicate to Allah?
He said: I have not yet finished supplicating to Him for my sins, so how can I supplicate for my eye (4) ?!
Ḥarīz ibn ʿUthmān: Rāshid ibn Saʿd narrated to us; he said: A man came to Abū ⟦2:349⟧ al-Dardāʾ and said: Give me counsel.
He said: Remember Allah in prosperity and He will remember you in adversity; when you remember the dead, count yourself as one of them; and when your soul looks eagerly at something of this world, consider what it will come to (1) .
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, from Hammām ibn al-Ḥārith:
Abū al-Dardāʾ was teaching a non-Arab man to recite: “Indeed, the tree of al-Zaqqūm is the food of the sinful” [al-Dukhān: 43], and he said: The food of the orphan.
He corrected him, but he was unable to say it, so he said: Say: the food of the wicked; and so he taught him to recite: the food of the wicked.
Manṣūr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Murrah:
That Abū al-Dardāʾ said: Worship Allah as though you see Him, count yourself among the dead, beware of the supplication of the wronged, and know that a little that suffices you is better than much that distracts you, that righteousness does not wear out, and that sin is not forgotten (2) .
شيبان: عن عاصم، عن أبي وائل، عن أبي الدرداء:
Beware of the supplications of the wronged, for they ascend to Allah like sparks of fire (3) .
Luqmān ibn ʿĀmir narrated that Abū al-Dardāʾ said:
The people of wealth eat and we eat, they drink and we drink, they dress and we dress, they ride and we ride; they have surplus wealth which they look at, and we look at it with them; their reckoning is upon it, and we are free of it (4) .
And from him, he said: Praise be to Allah, who has made the rich wish that they were like us at ⟦2:350⟧ death, while we do not wish that we were like them then. Our rich brothers have not been fair to us: they love us for the sake of religion and show enmity to us over the world (1) .
Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr al-Ḥimṣī narrated it from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr.
وروى: صفوان، عن ابن جبير، عن أبيه، قال:
When Cyprus was conquered, the captives were brought past Abū al-Dardāʾ, and he wept.
I said to him: You weep on a day like this, on which Allah has strengthened Islam and its people!
He said: O Jubayr! While this nation was dominant and supreme, they disobeyed Allah, and they met what you see. How insignificant the servants are to Allah when they disobey Him (2) .
بقية: عن حبيب بن عمر، عن أبي عبد الصمد، عن أم الدرداء، قالت:
Abū al-Dardāʾ would not narrate a hadith without smiling.
I said: I fear that people will think you a fool.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not narrate a hadith without smiling.
Aḥmad recorded it in (al-Musnad (3)) .
عكرمة بن عمار: عن أبي قدامة محمد بن عبيد، عن أم الدرداء، قالت:
Abū al-Dardāʾ had three hundred and sixty friends for the sake of Allah, for whom he would pray in his prayer. I spoke to him about that.
He said: There is no man who prays for his brother in his absence but Allah appoints two angels for him who say: And for you the like. Should I not then desire that the angels pray for me (4) ? ⟦2:351⟧
Abū al-Zāhiriyyah said: Abū al-Dardāʾ said: We smile in the faces of some people while our hearts curse them (1) .
Umm al-Dardāʾ said: When Abū al-Dardāʾ was on his deathbed, he began saying:
Who will work for the like of this day of mine? Who will work for the like of this resting-place of mine?
أخبرنا أبو المعالي أحمد بن إسحاق، أخبرنا الفتح بن عبد السلام، أخبرنا محمد بن عمر القاضي، ومحمد بن علي، ومحمد بن أحمد الطرائقي، قالوا:
أخبرنا محمد بن أحمد بن المسلمة، أخبرنا عبيد الله بن عبد الرحمن، أخبرنا جعفر الفريابي، حدثنا محمد بن عائذ، حدثنا الهيثم بن حميد، حدثنا الوضين بن عطاء، عن يزيد بن مزيد، قال:
The Dajjāl was mentioned in a gathering in which Abū al-Dardāʾ was present, and Nawf al-Bikālī (2) said: I fear something other than the Dajjāl more than I fear the Dajjāl.
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: And what is it?
He said: I fear that my faith will be stripped from me without my being aware of it.
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: May your mother be bereaved of you, O son of the Kindī woman! Are there on ⟦2:352⟧ the earth fifty who fear what you fear?
Then he said: Or thirty, or twenty, or ten, or five?
Then he said: Or three? Each time he said: May your mother be bereaved of you. By the One in whose hand my soul is, no servant has ever felt secure about his faith but it was stripped from him, or wrested from him, so that he loses it. By the One in whose hand my soul is, faith is nothing but like a shirt that one puts on at one time and takes off at another.
Al-Wāqidī, Abū Mushir and Ibn Numayr said: Abū al-Dardāʾ died in the year 32 AH (1) .
From Khālid ibn Maʿdān, who said: He died in the year 31 AH (2) .
This is an error, because al-Thawrī narrated from: الأعمش، عن عمارة بن عمير، عن حريث بن ظهير، قال:
When the news of the death —meaning of Ibn Masʿūd— reached Abū al-Dardāʾ, he said: He has not left behind anyone like him!
And ʿAbd Allāh's death was in the year 32 AH.
Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh narrated from Abū ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ashʿarī, who said:
Abū al-Dardāʾ died before the killing of ʿUthmān (may Allah be pleased with both of them) (3) .
It was said: Those in Abū al-Dardāʾ's circle for teaching recitation numbered more than a thousand men, each ten of them having an instructor, and Abū al-Dardāʾ would go round them standing; when one of them had mastered it, he would move over to Abū al-Dardāʾ —meaning: to recite to him for review.
From Abū al-Dardāʾ, who said: Whoever remembers death often, his joy diminishes and his envy diminishes. ⟦2:353⟧
